uncited: It builds on [Proxy Geometry and Slicing](15424-proxy-geometry-and-slicing.md) by dynamically regenerating geometry every frame to maintain view alignment.
The method renders the volume by intersecting parallel slicing planes with the volume bounding box, generating billboards that face the camera.
These billboards are rasterized, and fragment shaders sample the 3D volume texture at interpolated 3D texture coordinates.
*   **Inputs**: 3D volume data (scalar field), camera position (`eyePos`), view matrix (`mtx`), volume dimensions (`res`), and sampling rate (`sampleRate` or `numberOfSlices`).
The coordinates map the unit quad to the volume bounds.
It uses three stacks of 2D textures corresponding to these directions.
*   **Time Complexity**: $O(N \cdot S)$, where $N$ is the number of slices and $S$ is the number of fragments per slice (proportional to screen resolution).
View-aligned slicing emerged as a method to combine the quality of ray casting with the speed of rasterization.
